thesis: This is the first pack since 6/2 with hard, corroborated company facts rather than commentary, so the dry powder I have been holding since the 6/4 XOM exit gets deployed. Three separate items say the same thing from both sides of the deal: Nvidia signs a multi-year memory chip deal with SK Hynix, SK Hynix announces a multi-year tech deal with Nvidia for AI factories, and South Korea's Naver will build gigawatt-scale AI factories on Nvidia technology. That is a signed supply agreement plus a named customer build-out, and it directly retires the one bearish thread I flagged on 6/5, when automakers and retailers warned that a US memory-chip shortage was lifting prices: Nvidia has now locked in HBM supply rather than bidding for it spot. I add to NVDA, but I size the add at only 5 dollars rather than filling my cap, because NVDA already sits near 39% of equity against a 50% limit and good news on the name is exactly the case where the open gaps up and carries the position into that cap; at 5 dollars the position stays inside 50% even if NVDA opens 25% higher while QQQ and XLK open 5% lower, whereas a larger add would breach the cap on a 20% gap and cost me the entire batch, including the energy leg. Conviction expressed at a size that survives the validator beats conviction that gets rejected. Second, the energy trade is back on its original footing: oil prices rise as Iran and Israel trade strikes in defiance of Trump, with the silver and UK hiring items both attributing moves to the same escalation. I exited XOM on 6/4 because the pack then said a Lebanon deal was hitting oil; that premise has reversed on today's tape, and following the pack in both directions is the point, so I re-open a 12 dollar XOM sleeve, which carries no cap risk of its own at roughly 10% of equity, as the only non-tech leg in an otherwise all-tech book. I ignore the Ken Fisher 'top AI stock' pieces on NVDA, MSFT, GOOGL and AMZN, the 'should you buy' listicles on GS, CAT and XOM itself, and the SpaceX IPO chatter: those are aggregator content with no new fact, and the XOM entry rests on the oil-price item, not on the listicle that happens to share the ticker. After fills, cash falls to roughly 9 dollars, close to 8% of equity against my 5% floor, the largest name stays under the 50% cap, and the book holds 4 of 8 allowed positions.
